comp.done.nextSearch: Search the content of the case from the eDiscovery tab: the hold guarantees it is still there even if it gets deleted.
comp.done.rejectedBody: That part is NOT preserved. When the service is back, create another hold with the same reason and reference just for {services}.
comp.export.auditedBody: The download is recorded in the audit trail with your name, the date and whose content it is. From then on the file lives on your machine: keep it wherever your procedure requires and delete it when the case closes.
comp.export.auditedTitle: It is recorded and it leaves Sytue
comp.export.intro: This is not a listing: it is the full content, readable outside Sytue. Review what you are about to download.

comp.export.whatMail: All their email of the period, with attachments, in an .mbox file
comp.holds.descriptionActive: The ones preserving data right now.
comp.holds.descriptionAll: Active and already released. The released ones are kept as evidence of when preservation stopped.
comp.holds.emptyDescription: A hold preserves someone’s email and files for as long as a case lasts. It takes a minute to create and is released when the case closes.
comp.holds.title: Holds
comp.holds.whatBody: It freezes what is in an account for litigation: the person can keep deleting their email and files, but nothing is really removed until you release the hold. Creating and releasing them is privileged access and is recorded under your name.
comp.impact.auditedBody: Who creates it, when and why is recorded. That record is the proof that you preserved in time, so the reason matters.
comp.impact.auditedTitle: It is recorded under your name
comp.impact.noDeleteBody: While it is active, neither {subject} nor you nor any other administrator can permanently delete {what}. They can keep deleting whatever they like: a copy is kept that is only visible from eDiscovery.
comp.impact.orgWideBody: No account will be able to purge anything while the hold is active, and the space used can only grow. If the case points at specific people, go back and choose them: it is cheaper and easier to defend.
comp.impact.orgWideTitle: You are about to hold the whole organisation
comp.impact.releaseBody: You release it from the list and normal deletion resumes. Whatever was in the bin becomes purgeable.
comp.impact.releaseTitle: It is released when the case ends
comp.impact.silentBody: Their account works exactly the same and shows no notice. That is what procedures usually require: nobody must know that data is being preserved.
comp.impact.silentTitle: The person does not find out
comp.impact.whatForBody: For litigation, internal investigations and legal requirements: it freezes the evidence before anyone deletes it. It is not a backup and it is not for archiving.
comp.impact.whatForTitle: What a legal hold is for
comp.offline.all: We cannot reach Email, Files or Notepads
comp.offline.body: What you see may be incomplete and actions on that service will fail. Try again in a few minutes.

comp.reason.placeholder: Employment claim from a former employee, court order no. 4
comp.reason.required: Write why it is being held: this is what the audit trail will show.
comp.release.audited: The release is recorded with your name and the date. The hold is kept in the history (to see it: “Show released ones too”).
comp.release.confirm: Release and go back to normal deletion
comp.release.point1: The account’s normal deletion applies again.
comp.release.point2: Whatever is in the bin can be purged and stops appearing in eDiscovery.
comp.release.point3: What has already been purged cannot be recovered: if the case is still open, do not release it yet.

comp.review.startsNow: As soon as you create it
comp.scope.bothBody: The usual choice in litigation: nothing that account deletes really disappears, neither in the mailbox nor in Drive.
comp.scope.driveBody: Drive files are preserved. Email keeps being deleted as always, including what is already in the bin.
comp.scope.help: Whatever you do not tick here keeps being deleted as usual, so when in doubt preserve more: releasing later is instant, recovering what was purged is not.
comp.scope.mailBody: The mailbox is preserved. Drive files keep being deleted as always, including the ones already in the bin.
comp.scope.notesBody: Notepads notebooks are preserved. Email and Drive files keep being deleted as always, including what is already in the bin.
comp.scope.offlineBody: That part of the hold will fail. You can create it anyway (whatever does respond will be preserved) and repeat it later for what is missing.
comp.scope.title: What is preserved

gov.act.allowBody: It goes out as usual and no decision is recorded. It is there to make an exception to another, stricter rule.
gov.act.blockBody: The call does not leave Sytue. The integration gets an error and that feature of it stops working. Use it when that data must never leave.
gov.act.warn: Let it through, but tell you
gov.act.warnBody: The call goes out all the same and the integration keeps working, but it is recorded under “Decisions”. This is how you try a rule out before cutting anything off.
gov.applyNowOff: It will be saved switched off: you can prepare it now and switch it on from the list whenever you want.
gov.applyNowOn: It starts being evaluated on the next call to third parties.
gov.cond.all: all calls to third parties, without exception
gov.decisions.description: Every time a rule blocks or flags a call, it lands here. A block leaves no trace in the egress log (the call never went out): this is its only evidence.
gov.decisions.emptyDescription: Nothing has been blocked or flagged. When a rule acts on a call, you will see it here with its date and its destination.
gov.decisions.loadFailed: Could not load the decisions. Try again in a few seconds.
gov.decisions.offline: No connection to the gateway: the decisions cannot be loaded.
gov.decisions.title: What your rules have done
gov.delete.afterBlock: The traffic this rule was blocking goes out of Sytue as usual again. If you only want to pause it, switch it off from the list instead of deleting it: that way you keep the condition.
gov.delete.afterWarn: That traffic stops being recorded under “Decisions”. What is already logged is kept.
gov.done.checkBodyBlock: Open the “Decisions” tab in a while: there you will see every call the rule has blocked. If an integration that had to keep working shows up, switch the rule off from the list and narrow the condition.
gov.done.checkBodyWarn: Open the “Decisions” tab in a while: there you will see every call the rule has flagged. If an integration that had to keep working shows up, switch the rule off from the list and narrow the condition.
gov.done.off: It is saved but switched off: turn it on from the list whenever you want.
gov.done.on: It is already evaluated on every call to third parties: {what}.
gov.egress.description: Every call an integration has made to an outside service: where, when and how it answered. Metadata only, never the content or the credentials.
gov.egress.emptyDescription: There are no calls to third parties for that filter yet. As soon as an integration reaches the network, it appears here.
gov.egress.loadFailed: Could not load the log. Adjust the filters and try again.
gov.egress.offline: No connection to the gateway: the egress log cannot be loaded.

gov.field.body: A text inside what is sent
gov.field.bodyHelp: For data leaks: it acts if the sent content includes that word. It can only be inspected in small payloads, so do not use it as the only condition.
gov.field.familyHelp: The key of the template you connected the service with. Use it when the specific domain does not matter.
gov.field.hostHelp: The domain of the service, for example api.salesforce.com. If you start it with a dot (.salesforce.com) it covers every subdomain.
gov.field.methodHelp: GET only reads; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE write or delete. Leave it empty for any of them.
gov.field.pathHelp: The start of the path, in case you only want part of the service. Leave it empty for the whole API.
gov.impact.allowBody: Rules that let traffic through never break an integration: they only make an exception to a stricter one.
gov.impact.allowTitle: This rule cannot cut anything off
gov.impact.blockBody: These would have been blocked: {hosts}. If any belongs to an integration in use, that feature stops working as soon as you save. Create it as a warning first if you would rather check without breaking anything.

gov.impact.blockTitle.one: This rule would cut off traffic that is in use ({matched} of {count} call)
gov.impact.blockTitle.other: This rule would cut off traffic that is in use ({matched} of the last {count} calls)

gov.impact.noneBody.one: {count} call recorded, and it does not match this rule.
gov.impact.noneBody.other: None of the last {count} recorded calls match this rule.

gov.impact.noneTitle: Nothing that works today would be affected
gov.impact.unknownBody: The egress log is empty, so we do not know which integrations would be affected. If in doubt, create it as a warning and watch it for a few days before blocking.
gov.impact.upperBound: The count is an upper bound: the path and the content cannot be checked from the log.
gov.impact.warnBody: These would have been flagged: {hosts}. If any belongs to an integration in use, that feature stops working as soon as you save.

gov.impact.warnTitle.one: This rule would flag {matched} of {count} call

gov.rules.emptyDescription: Without rules, any connected integration can call wherever it likes. The one most people create first: warn when something is sent out, to see the real traffic before blocking anything.

labels.description: Mark files by how sensitive they are — public, internal, confidential — and decide which ones may not leave the organisation. Whoever works with the file sees the label; Sytue makes sure it is not shared outside if you said so.
labels.empty.description: Without labels every file is treated the same. The scale almost everyone starts with: Public, Internal and Confidential — and only the last one blocks sharing outside.

labels.manualNote: Labelling is manual: each person picks the label while working with the file. Sytue does not classify anything on its own.

wizard.accessPolicy.done.checkBodyExempt: Open a private browser window and sign in with an account the rule affects. That way you see the same as your team and confirm that you still have access with the exempt accounts ({names}).
wizard.accessPolicy.err.badCidr: “{range}” is not a valid network range. Write the network and its size: 203.0.113.0/24 for a whole office, or 198.51.100.7/32 for a single address.
wizard.accessPolicy.err.bothTimes: Give both times: from when and until when.
wizard.accessPolicy.exempt.description: This is your emergency exit: these accounts get in even when the rule matches. Exclude your administrators here so that you do not lock yourself out of the console.
wizard.accessPolicy.exempt.heading: Who is always exempt
wizard.accessPolicy.exempt.none: You have not left anybody exempt. If this rule ends up affecting you, you will be locked out and unable to undo it.
wizard.accessPolicy.exempt.some: Exempt: {names}. They will always be able to sign in.
wizard.accessPolicy.fix.badData: The service rejected one of the values. Check the network ranges in the “When” step.
wizard.accessPolicy.fix.forbidden: Your account does not have permission to change the access rules of this organisation.
wizard.accessPolicy.fix.idpDown: Sytue ID is not responding right now. Try again in a minute.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.description: This is what we are going to apply. You can change anything before saving.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.enableOff: It will be saved switched off: you can prepare it now and switch it on from the list whenever you want.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.enableOn: It will start being evaluated at the next sign-in.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.nameHint: This is how you will see it in the list. If you leave it empty we will call it “{suggested}”.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.priorityHint: It only changes the order in which the rules are checked: the lowest number goes first. You can move it later from the list with the arrows.
wizard.accessPolicy.review.understood: I understand that nobody will be able to sign in and I want to save it anyway
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.allowBody: Rules that let people through cannot shut you out: they only make exceptions to stricter ones.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.allowTitle: This rule cannot lock anybody out
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.hasExitBody: {sentence} Exempt: {exempt}. They will be able to sign in even when the rule matches. Check that you can sign in with one of those accounts before you leave.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.hasExitBodyMfa: {sentence} Exempt: {exempt}. They will be able to sign in even when the rule matches. Careful: anybody who has not set up two-step verification yet will have to set it up in order to sign in. Check that you can sign in with one of those accounts before you leave.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.lockoutBody: {sentence} Nobody would be able to sign in to Sytue again, you included, and you would not be able to get into this console to undo it either. Add a condition in the “When” step, or exclude your administrators in the “Who” step.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.lockoutTitle: This rule would lock out your whole organisation
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.noExitBody: {sentence} If it ever catches you, you will be locked out of the console and nobody will be able to put it right. Go back to the “Who” step and exclude your administrators group: they will still get in even when the rule matches.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.noExitBodyMfa: {sentence} If it ever catches you, you will be locked out of the console and nobody will be able to put it right. Careful: anybody who has not set up two-step verification yet will have to set it up in order to sign in. Go back to the “Who” step and exclude your administrators group: they will still get in even when the rule matches.
wizard.accessPolicy.risk.noExitTitle: You have not left an emergency exit
wizard.accessPolicy.sentence.always: With this rule, {who} {what} at every sign-in attempt.
wizard.accessPolicy.summary.stateOn: It will apply as soon as you save it
wizard.accessPolicy.summary.whenAlways: Whenever they try to sign in
wizard.accessPolicy.what.allow: will sign in with no further checks
wizard.accessPolicy.what.block: will not be able to sign in
wizard.accessPolicy.what.description: Choose what the person finds when the rule matches.
wizard.accessPolicy.what.heading: What do you want to happen in those cases?
wizard.accessPolicy.what.mfa: will have to confirm their identity with a second factor
wizard.accessPolicy.what.strictestWins: If several rules match at once, the strictest one wins: blocking beats asking for verification, and asking for verification beats letting through.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.appsHint: Identifiers of the applications, separated by spaces. Leave it empty to apply it to all of them (the most common choice).
wizard.accessPolicy.when.description: Tick only what you need. If you tick nothing, the rule applies whenever those people try to sign in.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.deviceBody: Each person marks their usual devices as trusted under “Devices”. With this switched on, the rule only acts when they sign in from one they have not marked: a borrowed computer, a new phone, an internet café.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.deviceSwitch: Only when the device is not trusted
wizard.accessPolicy.when.heading: In which situations does it apply?
wizard.accessPolicy.when.insideBody: It only applies to whoever connects from those networks. Useful together with the “let them through, full stop” action.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.insideTitle: When they are INSIDE those networks
wizard.accessPolicy.when.networkBody: Write the networks you know (your office, the VPN…) and choose whether the rule should act inside or outside them.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.networksHint: One per line. Whoever runs your company network can give them to you. Leave it empty not to look at the network.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.outsideBody: This is the usual one: protecting what happens away from the office (home, hotels, public networks).
wizard.accessPolicy.when.outsideTitle: When they are OUTSIDE those networks
wizard.accessPolicy.when.soFarNone: With no conditions, the rule will apply whenever those people try to sign in.
wizard.accessPolicy.when.timeBody: Leave the days unticked and the times empty not to look at the calendar. The times are in UTC, not in each person’s local time.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.allBody: It applies to anybody who signs in to your organisation.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.description: Start by deciding who it applies to. Below you can leave out the people it must never affect.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.heading: Who does this rule affect?
wizard.accessPolicy.who.noGroups: There are no groups in your organisation yet.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.noUsers: There are no users to show.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.nobodyYet: nobody yet (you have not chosen who)
wizard.accessPolicy.who.pickAtLeastOne: Choose at least one group or one person, or go back to “Everybody”.
wizard.accessPolicy.who.someBody: It applies only to whoever you choose. Nobody else notices it.
wizard.app.choose.description: Pick one of the applications your team already uses. We guide you through the rest: you do not have to know about SSO or SCIM.
wizard.app.choose.heading: Which application do you want to connect?
wizard.app.choose.noResults: No application is called that. Try another name.
wizard.app.configure.description: Only the essentials. Under every field we tell you where to find it, and we check what you type as you go.
wizard.app.configure.heading: Your {app} values
wizard.app.configure.nameError: Give it a name so you can recognise it.
wizard.app.configure.nameHint: It is only shown here, in the console. You can keep the one we suggest.
wizard.app.configure.secretStored: It is stored encrypted and never shown again: not even we can read it. If it ever changes, you replace it with a new one.
wizard.app.done.heading: {app} is now connected
wizard.app.done.oidcBody: Paste these credentials into the OIDC sign-in settings of {app}.
wizard.app.done.oidcTitle: Copy them now: they are not shown again
wizard.app.done.okBody: The connection is active and your team already has it available.
wizard.app.done.samlBody: Register this address in the SSO settings of {app}.
wizard.app.done.step1Body: Open the Sytue app launcher: {app} shows up next to the rest of the suite for everybody who has access.
wizard.app.done.step1Title: Check that it appears in the portal
wizard.app.done.step2Body: Go into {app} with your Sytue account. If it lets you through without asking for an {app} password, it is set up correctly.
wizard.app.done.step2BodyLaunch: Go into {app} from the button below with your Sytue account. If it lets you through without asking for an {app} password, it is set up correctly.
wizard.app.done.step3Body: The first synchronisation starts on its own. From the {app} card you can check the status or force another one.
wizard.app.effect.dataBody: Sytue will be able to read data from {app} for reports. It never writes or deletes anything.
wizard.app.effect.portalBody: Your team will see {app} among their applications when they sign in to Sytue.
wizard.app.effect.scimBody: When somebody joins or leaves your organisation, their {app} account is created or disabled on its own.
wizard.app.effect.ssoBody: No separate password is needed for {app}: people sign in with their Sytue account and your access rules apply.
wizard.app.effect.ssoTitle: They sign in with their Sytue account
wizard.app.err.noPath: Only the name or the domain, with no slashes and no paths.
wizard.app.err.noScheme: Write it without “https://”, just the name.
wizard.app.err.required: We need this value to carry on.
wizard.app.explain.description: None of this applies yet: first you configure it and test it.
wizard.app.explain.heading: This is what you will switch on in {app}
wizard.app.explain.needTitle: Have this to hand before you carry on
wizard.app.fix.activateBadData: Check the values in the “Configure” step: we could not register the sign-in.
wizard.app.fix.activateGeneric: Something went wrong along the way. Try again.
wizard.app.fix.activateIdpDown: Sytue ID is not responding right now. Try again in a minute.
wizard.app.fix.badData: The values do not add up. Check “{field}” in the previous step.
wizard.app.fix.down: {app} is not responding right now. It is not your values: try again in a minute.
wizard.app.fix.generic: We could not connect. Review the values in the previous step and try again.
wizard.app.fix.notFound: We could not find that {app} account. Check “{field}”: it is usually a typo.
wizard.app.fix.rejected: {app} rejected the connection. Check that the application allows access from Sytue.
wizard.app.fix.rejectedSecret: {app} rejected the “{secret}”: it may have expired or may not have enough permissions. Generate a new one and paste it again.
wizard.app.need.fieldWhere: You will find it in the settings of your {app} account.
wizard.app.need.secretWhere: It is generated in the {app} admin panel. You need administrator permissions there.
wizard.app.oauth.body: We will take you to {app} so that you can approve the access. You do not have to create or paste any credential.
wizard.app.oauth.revocable: The permission expires on its own and you can withdraw it whenever you want, from here or from {app}.
wizard.app.oauth.title: Connect with your {app} account
wizard.app.review.description: This is what we are going to apply. You can change anything before you carry on.
wizard.app.review.heading: Review and activate
wizard.app.review.note: Once activated, {app} appears in your team’s portal and we register the sign-in. You can deactivate it whenever you want: nothing is deleted inside {app}.
wizard.app.summary.name: Name of the connection
wizard.app.test.description: It is a test call with the values you entered. Nothing is switched on for your team yet.
wizard.app.test.heading: Let us check that Sytue reaches {app}
wizard.app.test.idleHelp: Press “Test connection” and we verify the values against {app}. If something does not add up, we tell you exactly what to change.
wizard.app.test.okBody: We talked to {app} and it answered. You can activate it now.
wizard.app.test.skipHint: You can carry on without testing, but it is better to check now.
wizard.auto.connect.description: You approve the permissions on their screen. We only ever read; we never write to the service you are leaving.
wizard.auto.connect.heading: Sign in to {source}
wizard.auto.connect.readOnly: Read-only access. You can revoke it whenever you want, from here or from the provider.
wizard.auto.connect.readOnlyGithub: GitHub has no read-only permission for private repositories: the one it offers (repo) also allows writing. Sytue only ever reads, and the permission is yours to revoke at any moment from GitHub.
wizard.auto.delegation.microsoftBody: Open the Microsoft screen we link below with an administrator account and approve it. That is the whole step: the same application then reads the organisation, with the same read-only permissions.

wizard.auto.delegation.readyBody.one: We can now bring across the content of {count} person.
wizard.auto.delegation.readyBody.other: We can now bring across the content of {count} people.

wizard.auto.delegation.step1: In the Google Cloud console, create a service account and download its JSON key.
wizard.auto.delegation.step2: Paste that JSON here and save it.
wizard.auto.delegation.step3: Open the Google screen we link below: the client and the permissions come pre-filled, so you only have to authorise.
wizard.auto.delegation.title: One extra permission for the whole organisation
wizard.auto.delegation.why: The key is stored encrypted and is only used to read, on behalf of each person, what belongs to them.
wizard.auto.delegation.whyMicrosoft: Approving it does not give Sytue anything new: they are the same read permissions, now for the organisation instead of just your account. An administrator can revoke it in Entra whenever they want.
wizard.auto.error.connect: We could not start the sign-in. Try again in a few seconds.
wizard.auto.error.launch: We could not launch the import. Try again in a few seconds.
wizard.auto.error.noKek: This deployment has no encryption key configured, so it cannot store what {source} would hand back. An operator has to set it up.
wizard.auto.error.noProviderApp: Sytue is not registered as an app with {source} yet, so there is no sign-in to send you to. An operator adds it under Platform administration → Third-party connections; until then, retrying changes nothing.
wizard.auto.error.plan: We could not check what there is. The sign-in may have expired: sign in again.
wizard.auto.error.serviceKey: We could not save that key. Check that it is the full JSON of the service account.
wizard.auto.error.title: That did not work
wizard.auto.limits.title: What does not come across
wizard.auto.nots.actions: GitHub Actions runs and their logs. The workflow files travel with the code; the run history stays behind.
wizard.auto.nots.cloudDatabases: Databases (Cloud SQL, Firestore, BigQuery). They cannot be copied through a control API: they have to be exported and restored, and you decide when writes stop. We list every one of them with what to do about it.
wizard.auto.nots.cloudImages: Container images already running on Google. Sytue DevX builds from your repository: connect it to the project and the first deployment replaces them.
wizard.auto.nots.forgeAccount: People who have never signed in to Sytue Git yet. Their repositories wait until they sign in once; then you resume the job.
wizard.auto.nots.settings: Repository settings that only exist on GitHub: branch protection, secrets, apps and webhooks.
wizard.auto.nots.teamsGuests: Guests from other organisations, and channels shared with them: they have no account here, so we leave them out instead of inventing one.
wizard.auto.nots.teamsHistory: Teams messages are not republished in Rooms. Rooms posts a message as whoever writes it now, so putting them there would fake either the author or the date. Each channel’s history travels as a faithful transcript in Drive, with the real author and date inside.
wizard.auto.origin.description: Pick the service. The only thing we will ask you for is to sign in to it.
wizard.auto.origin.heading: What are you moving away from?
wizard.auto.review.description: Nothing has been copied yet. Once you launch it, the copy runs in the background and you can close this page.
wizard.auto.review.heading: This is what we bring

wizard.auto.review.jobsValue.one: {count} (one per person and type of content)
wizard.auto.review.jobsValue.other: {count} (one per person and type of content)

wizard.auto.review.people.one: {count} person, each in their own account
wizard.auto.review.people.other: {count} people, each in their own account

wizard.auto.safe.body: We only read. The service you are leaving stays exactly as it is, and you can run this again: whatever has already been copied is not duplicated.
wizard.auto.safe.title: Nothing is lost at the source
wizard.auto.scope.mineHint: Everything the account you sign in with owns. One sign-in and nothing else — this is the usual choice, and every other person can do the same for themselves.
wizard.auto.scope.orgHint: Google does not let one sign-in read other people’s content, so for the whole company it asks for one extra permission. We take you straight to the screen where you grant it.
wizard.auto.scope.orgHintMicrosoft: One sign-in only opens your own content. For the whole company, an administrator approves a single screen — no service accounts and nothing to paste. We take you straight there.
wizard.auto.source.githubDesc: Your repositories go to Sytue Git with their history, branches, tags, issues, pull requests, wiki and releases. Your gists go to Sytue Drive.
wizard.auto.source.googleDesc: Your files and contacts, your Gmail, your calendar and your Google Cloud and Firebase apps. You sign in once and we read them; nothing changes on Google.
wizard.auto.source.microsoftDesc: Your OneDrive and your contacts, and your Microsoft Teams: teams, channels and members go to Sytue Rooms, and each channel’s files and conversation history go to Sytue Drive.

wizard.auto.unmatched.body.one: {count} account from the old service has no equivalent in Sytue, so we leave it out rather than copy it into the wrong mailbox. Create that person in the directory and run this again.
wizard.auto.unmatched.body.other: {count} accounts from the old service have no equivalent in Sytue, so we leave them out rather than copy them into the wrong mailbox. Create those people in the directory and run this again.

wizard.auto.unmatched.title: Accounts we cannot match
wizard.idp.configure.description: Under every field we tell you where to find it, and we check what you type as you go.
wizard.idp.done.pasteOidc: Your provider will only return your team to Sytue if this address is registered in the application you created.
wizard.idp.done.pasteSaml: Register it in your SAML application: without this, your provider does not know where to reply.
wizard.idp.done.pasteTitle: Paste this into your provider’s settings
wizard.idp.done.savedOff: The provider is saved but disabled. Enable it from the list once you have finished the step below.
wizard.idp.done.savedOn: The provider is enabled. As soon as you complete the step below, your team will be able to sign in with the company account.
wizard.idp.done.step1Oidc: In your app registration, under redirect URI (web type). Paste it exactly, with no extra trailing slash.
wizard.idp.done.step1Saml: In your SAML application, under “Reply URL” and “Identifier”. Paste them exactly.
wizard.idp.done.step1Title: Register the values above in your provider
wizard.idp.done.step2Body: Open a private browser window, go to the Sytue sign-in screen and use “Sign in with your organisation”. If you get in without us asking for a Sytue password, it is set up correctly.
wizard.idp.done.step2Title: Try it with your own account
wizard.idp.done.step3Body: From now on they sign in with the company account. Anyone who already had a Sytue password can carry on using it.
wizard.idp.effect.noLossBody: Anyone who already has a Sytue password can carry on using it. This adds a way in, it does not replace one.
wizard.idp.effect.offBody: You configure it, you test it and you enable it at the end. Until then, nobody sees it on the sign-in screen.
wizard.idp.effect.offTitle: Nothing is switched on until you say so
wizard.idp.effect.signInBody: Your team will use the “Sign in with your organisation” button and their usual company password. One less to remember.
wizard.idp.effect.signInTitle: They sign in with the company account
wizard.idp.effect.whoBody: You can restrict access to your organisation’s email domains, even if your provider holds more people.
wizard.idp.err.badDomain: This does not look like a domain: “{domain}”. Write it without “@” or “https://”, just acme.com.
wizard.idp.err.badIssuerUrl: That address is not valid. Check it: it is usually a typo.
wizard.idp.err.badUrl: That address is not valid. Check it.
wizard.idp.err.certRequired: We need the provider’s signing certificate.
wizard.idp.err.hasSpace: A space slipped in. Paste the address only.
wizard.idp.err.insecure: It has to start with https:// (that http:// is not secure).
wizard.idp.err.mustBeHttps: It has to be an https:// address.
wizard.idp.err.nameRequired: Give it a name so you can recognise it.
wizard.idp.err.needHttps: Write it in full, starting with https://
wizard.idp.err.noDomain: The domain is missing: check the address.
wizard.idp.err.notCert: This does not look like a certificate. Paste it exactly as your provider gives it to you, including the “-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----” lines.
wizard.idp.err.slugFormat: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (no spaces or accents).
wizard.idp.err.slugTaken: Another provider already uses this identifier.
wizard.idp.err.wellKnown: Remove the trailing “/.well-known/openid-configuration”: only the part before it goes here.
wizard.idp.err.xmlFormat: This does not look like the metadata XML: it must contain “EntityDescriptor”. Paste it whole, exactly as your provider gives it to you.
wizard.idp.err.xmlRequired: Paste here the metadata you download from your provider.
wizard.idp.explain.description: None of this applies yet: first you configure it and test it.
wizard.idp.explain.heading: This is what will change for your team
wizard.idp.explain.needTitle: Have this to hand before you carry on
wizard.idp.field.advancedHint: You do not need to touch any of this unless your provider uses names other than the standard ones.
wizard.idp.field.certHint: It is public: it is what proves the response really comes from your provider. Download it from the same screen.
wizard.idp.field.clientIdHint: Your provider gives it to you when you register the application (“Application (client) ID” in Entra ID).
wizard.idp.field.domainsHint: Only people whose email is in these domains will get in. Separate them with commas. Empty = anyone your provider lets through.
wizard.idp.field.entityHint: Also called “Azure AD Identifier” or “Issuer”. It usually looks like a web address.
wizard.idp.field.issuerHint: The base address, without “/.well-known/openid-configuration” at the end. Google Workspace: https://accounts.google.com
wizard.idp.field.issuerOk: Looks right. We will check it in the next step.
wizard.idp.field.name: Name
wizard.idp.field.nameHint: This is what your team sees on the sign-in button. Your provider’s name will do.
wizard.idp.field.noXmlLink: My provider does not give me the XML
wizard.idp.field.secretHint: Leave it empty only if your provider does not give you one (public application with PKCE).
wizard.idp.field.secretKeepHint: Leave it empty to keep the one you already have saved.
wizard.idp.field.secretStored: It is stored encrypted and never shown again, neither to you nor to us. If it ever expires, you type a new one here and that is that.
wizard.idp.field.slugHint: Short internal name, used in the sign-in addresses. We suggest one from the name.
wizard.idp.field.ssoUrlHint: The address we send your team to so that they can identify themselves (“SAML SSO endpoint”).
wizard.idp.field.useXmlLink: I would rather paste the metadata XML
wizard.idp.field.xmlHint: Download it from your provider (“federation metadata XML”) and paste it whole. We extract the rest.
wizard.idp.field.xmlOk: Looks right. We will take the address and the certificate from here.
wizard.idp.fix.forbidden: Your account does not have permission to configure sign-in in this organisation.
wizard.idp.fix.generic: We could not check it. Review the values in the previous step and try again.
wizard.idp.fix.idpDown: Sytue ID is not responding right now. It is not your values: try again in a minute.
wizard.idp.fix.oidcDiscovery: We could not read the configuration at that address. It is almost always the provider address: copy it again from your provider and remove the trailing “/.well-known/openid-configuration”.
wizard.idp.fix.samlData: The provider values do not add up. Check the Entity ID, that the sign-on URL starts with https:// and that the certificate is complete (with its BEGIN and END lines).
wizard.idp.fix.slugTaken: Another provider in your organisation already uses that identifier. Change the identifier in the previous step.
wizard.idp.kind.bothBody: Choose OpenID Connect: it takes fewer values to set up and there are no certificates to renew every few years.
wizard.idp.kind.oidcBlurb: What almost every provider uses today. They give you an address and two keys, and that is it.
wizard.idp.kind.oidcExamples: Microsoft Entra ID · Google Workspace · Okta · Auth0 · Keycloak
wizard.idp.kind.samlBlurb: The classic enterprise standard. Your provider gives you a metadata XML (or a certificate and two addresses).
wizard.idp.kind.samlExamples: AD FS · Okta or OneLogin in SAML mode · legacy providers
wizard.idp.mapping.hint: Leave the fields empty and we will use the standard names (email, name, groups).
wizard.idp.mapping.legend: Where we take each person’s details from
wizard.idp.need.client: The client ID and its secret
wizard.idp.need.clientWhere: They are created when you register an application in your provider (in Entra ID, “App registrations” → New registration → “Certificates & secrets”). Copy the secret as soon as you create it: almost every provider shows it only once.
wizard.idp.need.domainsWhere: The ones your team’s addresses use, for example acme.com. You can give several.
wizard.idp.need.issuerWhere: Microsoft Entra ID: your app registration → “Endpoints” → copy the OpenID Connect metadata document and remove the trailing “/.well-known/openid-configuration”. Google Workspace: it is https://accounts.google.com. Okta: https://your-company.okta.com.
wizard.idp.need.samlManual: Or else: Entity ID, sign-on URL and certificate
wizard.idp.need.samlManualWhere: They are on that same screen, one by one, in case your provider does not let you download the XML. The certificate is the provider’s signing certificate (it starts with “-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----”).
wizard.idp.need.samlXmlWhere: In your provider’s SAML application: “Download federation metadata XML” in Microsoft Entra ID, “Identity Provider metadata” in Okta. It is the quick way: you paste it and we fill in the rest for you.
wizard.idp.review.description: This is what we are going to apply. You can change anything before you carry on.
wizard.idp.review.enableLabel: Allow access with this provider straight away
wizard.idp.review.enableOff: It will be saved disabled: nobody sees it until you enable it from the list.
wizard.idp.review.enableOn: The “Sign in with your organisation” button will appear on your team’s sign-in screen.
wizard.idp.review.pendingOidc: When you save we give you the return address you have to register in your provider. Without it, signing in will not work.
wizard.idp.review.pendingSaml: When you save we give you the reply URL (ACS) and the Sytue identifier, which you have to register in your SAML application. Without them, signing in will not work.
wizard.idp.review.pendingTitle: One step is left in YOUR provider
wizard.idp.summary.fromXml: We read them from the metadata XML you pasted
wizard.idp.summary.name: Name
wizard.idp.summary.secretKept: The one you already had is kept
wizard.idp.summary.testFail: Failed (you can save anyway and fix it later)
wizard.idp.test.descriptionOidc: We ask your provider for its configuration. Nobody signs in yet.
wizard.idp.test.descriptionSaml: We check the Entity ID, the sign-on address and the certificate. Nobody signs in yet.
wizard.idp.test.draftNote: To be able to check it we saved it disabled. Nobody can sign in through it until you enable it in the next step.
wizard.idp.test.headingOidc: Let us check that Sytue reaches your provider
wizard.idp.test.headingSaml: Let us check your provider’s values
wizard.idp.test.idleHelp: Press “Check” and we verify the values you entered. If something does not add up, we tell you exactly what to change.
wizard.idp.test.okOidc: Your provider answered us and we read its configuration.
wizard.idp.test.okOidcPkce: Your provider answered us and we read its configuration (with PKCE, the safest mode).
wizard.idp.test.okSaml: The provider values are valid: the certificate reads correctly and the sign-on address is right.
wizard.idp.test.skipHint: You can carry on without checking, but it is better to catch a typo now.
wizard.idp.type.description: This is the only technical thing we will ask you. If you do not know, look for your provider’s name in the examples.
wizard.idp.type.heading: What does your identity provider connect with?
wizard.label.done.bodyBlock: It can already be chosen when classifying files. Those that carry it will not be shareable by public link.
wizard.label.done.bodyInform: It can already be chosen when classifying files. It only informs: it does not prevent sharing.
wizard.label.effect.blockBody: Nobody will be able to create a public link for a file with this label, and whoever tries will see the reason. Links that already existed will stop opening those files. Sharing with people or groups of your organisation keeps working the same.
wizard.label.effect.description: Choose by what really happens when somebody tries to share the file.
wizard.label.effect.heading: What should this label prevent?
wizard.label.effect.informBody: The label is shown next to the file so people know what they have in their hands, but it prevents nothing. It is the option for “Public” or “Internal”.
wizard.label.effect.summaryBlock: Prevents sharing the file outside the organisation
wizard.label.effect.warnBody: If your team already shares these files with customers or suppliers by link, warn them: as soon as you label a file, its link stops working.
wizard.label.level.description: Place it on your scale. It only serves to order them from least to most delicate; on its own it does not change what can be done with the files.
wizard.label.level.first: It is the first label of your organisation
wizard.label.level.firstBody: When you create more, you will be able to place them above or below this one.
wizard.label.level.heading: How sensitive is it, compared with the others?
wizard.label.level.hintHighest: They will use it for the most delicate things.
wizard.label.level.hintLowest: They will use it for the most open things.
wizard.label.level.scale: Your current scale, from least to most sensitive: {scale}.
wizard.label.review.description: This is what we are going to save. You can change anything beforehand.
wizard.label.review.editNoteBody: A file keeps the label exactly as it was when it was applied. If you change the name or what it prevents, what is already labelled stays as it was: that way a file classified a year ago still reads the same. To update it, label it again.
wizard.label.review.editNoteTitle: Files already labelled do not change
wizard.label.review.newNoteBody: The label will appear to choose from when classifying files in Sytue Drive. Labelling is manual: nothing is classified on its own.
wizard.label.summary.name: Name
wizard.label.toast.nameTaken: You already have a label with that name. Choose another one.
wizard.label.toast.retry: Try again in a few seconds.
wizard.label.what.colourHint: It only helps to recognise it at a glance in the lists.
wizard.label.what.description: Everybody will see the name and the explanation when labelling a file. Write them as you would tell someone who starts today.
wizard.label.what.heading: What is it called and what is it for?
wizard.label.what.nameHint: Short and recognisable. The most common ones: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
wizard.label.what.purposeHint: Optional, but strongly recommended: it is the clue that decides whether somebody uses it well.
wizard.label.what.purposePlaceholder: Business information that must not leave the company: contracts, payroll, customer data.
wizard.migrate.empty.description: To bring content over from Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace you have to connect it in Integrations. It is done once and serves the whole organisation.
wizard.migrate.empty.title: Connect the source first
wizard.migrate.error.forbidden: Your account is not allowed to migrate content in this organisation.
wizard.migrate.error.generic: We could not launch the migration. Try again in a few seconds.
wizard.migrate.error.sourceGone: The source connection no longer exists. Go back to Integrations and check it.
wizard.migrate.gets.contacts: Contacts with their name, their email addresses, their phone numbers and their organisation.
wizard.migrate.gets.files: The folders and the files, with their name and in the same path they had.
wizard.migrate.limits.description: We would rather tell you now than leave you a surprise two hours in.
wizard.migrate.limits.heading: This is what arrives and this is what does not
wizard.migrate.limits.safeBody: We only read. Your Microsoft 365 or your Google Workspace stay exactly as they are, and you can launch the migration again: what is already copied is not duplicated.
wizard.migrate.limits.safeTitle: Nothing is lost at the source
wizard.migrate.nots.googleNative: Google’s own documents (Docs, Sheets, Slides). They are not files: they have to be exported first. They are skipped one by one and we tell you which ones.
wizard.migrate.nots.mailCalendar: Email and calendar. They are not migrated yet; they will come later.
wizard.migrate.nots.modifiedDate: The original modification date: in Sytue everything will show today’s date. The content and the path are kept.
wizard.migrate.nots.namelessContacts: Contacts without any visible name: Sytue Contacts requires a name.
wizard.migrate.nots.permissions: The permissions and shared items of the source: each person gets their own.
wizard.migrate.nots.tooBig: Files over 2 GiB. They are skipped whole; they are never uploaded half-way.
wizard.migrate.origin.connection: We will read the content with the “{name}” connection, the one your organisation already uses.
wizard.migrate.origin.description: We use the connection you already configured in Integrations. There is nothing to install.
wizard.migrate.origin.heading: Where do we bring the content from?
wizard.migrate.origin.noneBody: To bring your content over, Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace has to be connected in Integrations first. It is a five-step wizard and it is only done once.
wizard.migrate.origin.noneTitle: There is no source connection yet
wizard.migrate.out.authBody: The connection used to bring content in can only read. To take it out, {provider} will ask you for permission to create files, contacts, mail and calendars in the account. If you already allowed it, just continue.
wizard.migrate.out.authFailed: We could not open the authorisation. Try again in a few seconds.
wizard.migrate.out.description: Pick the destination connection. We write with the permission that account granted, and only into a folder created by Sytue.
wizard.migrate.out.heading: Which account are you taking it to?
wizard.migrate.out.noticeBody: This COPIES to the destination account: nothing is deleted from Sytue. Files land in a “Sytue” folder on the destination Drive or OneDrive — they are not mixed with what is already there — and contacts are added to its address book. If the job is interrupted, it resumes where it left off and does not duplicate anything.
wizard.migrate.out.whatHeading: What are you taking with you?
wizard.migrate.out.whoDescription: For every person you pick, their own content is copied to the destination account. You can pick one or several.
wizard.migrate.review.description: Once launched, the copy runs in the background. You can close this page.
wizard.migrate.review.heading: Review and launch
wizard.migrate.review.ownAccountBody: The content never passes through your account. Sytue asks for permission to write on behalf of each person, that permission lasts minutes and is recorded in the audit trail.
wizard.migrate.review.ownAccountTitle: Each person gets theirs in THEIR account
wizard.migrate.self.conflict: It is already being copied. If it looks stuck, stop it and launch it again: it continues where it left off.
wizard.migrate.self.description: Choose the destination connection. It will write with the permission that account allowed.
wizard.migrate.self.gets.calendar: Calendars and their events, with their repeats and exceptions.
wizard.migrate.self.gets.mail: Mail with its folders, dates and attachments.
wizard.migrate.self.noticeBody: This COPIES to the destination account: nothing is deleted from Sytue. Files land in a “Sytue” folder, mail in the folder it belongs to (inbox, sent…) and each calendar arrives as a new one. If the copy stops, launch it again: it picks up where it was and does not duplicate anything.
wizard.migrate.self.nots.invites: Invitations: nobody gets notified. In Outlook, attendees are listed in the event description.
wizard.migrate.self.nots.outlookDrafts: In Outlook, a message with more than 3 MB of attachments arrives marked as a draft. It arrives whole: that is the only way Microsoft accepts large attachments.
wizard.migrate.self.nots.outlookRepeats: In Outlook, cancelled events and repeats it cannot represent. They are skipped one by one and we tell you which.
wizard.migrate.self.reviewBody: Sytue reads your content just like when you download “Your data” and writes it to {provider} with the permission you allowed. You can close this page: the copy keeps going in the background.
wizard.migrate.self.safeBody: We only read from Sytue: nothing changes here. If you launch the copy again, it brings what is new and does not duplicate what already arrived.

wizard.migrate.what.description: You can launch the rest later: each thing goes on its own.
wizard.migrate.what.driveHint: The folders and files of the personal drive, with the same structure.

wizard.migrate.who.description: Each person gets their own IN THEIR OWN Sytue account. You can choose one or several.

wizard.migrate.who.pickHelp: Tick whose content you want to migrate. If there are few of you, start with one person and check the result before launching the rest.
wizard.migrate.who.sourceHint: We put their Sytue email by default. Change it if they had a different address in {product}.

wizard.migrate.who.sourceTitle.other: Which account it is copied from ({count} people)

wizard.oidc.app.description: With this, your team will be able to sign in to it with their Sytue account, with no extra password.
wizard.oidc.app.heading: Which application do you want to connect?
wizard.oidc.app.nameHint: Only so that you recognise it here. You can use the name your team uses.
wizard.oidc.app.whereHint: If in doubt, choose the first one: that is the normal case for tools installed on a server.
wizard.oidc.done.heading: {name} can now use Sytue
wizard.oidc.done.pasteBody: Almost all of them ask only for the first two: with the Sytue address they fill in the rest themselves. If yours asks for each address separately, they are below.
wizard.oidc.done.secretBody: Paste it into the application next to the client identifier. If you lose it, generate a new one from the list (the previous one stops working).
wizard.oidc.done.secretTitle: Copy the secret now: it will not be shown again
wizard.oidc.done.separateTitle: Individual addresses (if your application asks for them one by one)
wizard.oidc.done.step1Body: Look in it for the OpenID Connect (or OAuth) sign-in section and fill it in with the Sytue address and the client identifier.
wizard.oidc.done.step1BodySecret: Look in it for the OpenID Connect (or OAuth) sign-in section and fill it in with the Sytue address, the client identifier and the secret.
wizard.oidc.done.step1Title: Paste the values above into the application
wizard.oidc.done.step2Body: Open a private browser window and go into the application with the sign-in-with-Sytue button. If it brings you back to the application already identified, it is ready.
wizard.oidc.done.step2Title: Try it with your own account
wizard.oidc.done.step3Body: From now on they sign in with their Sytue account. If somebody leaves the organisation, they lose access to this application automatically.
wizard.oidc.effect.controlBody: If somebody leaves the organisation, they stop getting into the application. And you can withdraw access to the whole application whenever you want.
wizard.oidc.effect.minimalBody: Name, email and identifier. Nothing else: not your documents, not your email, not your files.
wizard.oidc.effect.minimalTitle: The application only sees the basics
wizard.oidc.effect.signInBody: A sign-in button that leads to Sytue will appear in the application. Nobody needs a separate password.
wizard.oidc.effect.signInTitle: Your team signs in with their Sytue account
wizard.oidc.err.hasSpace: “{url}” has a space in it. Paste the address only.
wizard.oidc.err.insecure: It has to start with https:// (http:// is only accepted on localhost, for testing).
wizard.oidc.err.nameRequired: Give it a name so you can recognise it in the list.
wizard.oidc.err.noDomain: “{url}” is missing the domain. Check it.
wizard.oidc.err.noFragment: Remove everything after “#”: that part never reaches the server and is not valid here.
wizard.oidc.err.noWildcards: Wildcards (*) are not allowed. Write the exact address: that is what stops a third party from slipping in.
wizard.oidc.err.notUrl: “{url}” is not a valid address. It has to start with https:// and include the domain.
wizard.oidc.err.notWeb: “{url}” is not a web address. It must start with https://
wizard.oidc.err.redirectRequired: We need at least one return address.
wizard.oidc.fix.badUrls: Sytue ID rejected one of the addresses. Go over them: they have to start with https://, with no “#” and no wildcards.
wizard.oidc.fix.forbidden: Your account does not have permission to register applications in this organisation.
wizard.oidc.fix.generic: We could not register it. Review the values and try again.
wizard.oidc.fix.idpDown: Sytue ID is not responding right now. It is not your values: try again in a minute.
wizard.oidc.google.body: For apps written for Google Calendar, Drive, Contacts or the Workspace directory: they ask for Google permissions and get Sytue data. Google is not involved and sees nothing. Everyone who signs in to the app gives it this access to their data.
wizard.oidc.google.directoryHint: Read only, and only when the person signing in to the app administers the organisation.
wizard.oidc.google.title: Data access as a Google account
wizard.oidc.kind.browserBlurb: All its code sits on the user’s device, so it cannot keep secrets. It will use PKCE, which is just as safe for this case.
wizard.oidc.kind.browserExamples: A website built with React or Vue · an iOS or Android app · a desktop app
wizard.oidc.kind.browserTitle: An application that runs in the browser or on a phone
wizard.oidc.kind.serverBlurb: The application runs on a server and can keep a password secret. We will give it one.
wizard.oidc.kind.serverExamples: Grafana · GitLab · Jenkins · Nextcloud · an in-house tool with a backend
wizard.oidc.kind.serverTitle: An application with its own server
wizard.oidc.review.description: Nothing has been created yet. You can change anything before you carry on.
wizard.oidc.review.heading: Review and register
wizard.oidc.review.pkceBody: An application that runs on the user’s device cannot keep secrets. It will use PKCE, which protects the exchange without needing one.
wizard.oidc.review.pkceTitle: No secret, and that is fine
wizard.oidc.review.secretBody: When you register it we give you a password for the application. We do not store it in the clear and we will not be able to show it to you again: copy it there and then. If it gets lost, you generate another one from the list and that is that.
wizard.oidc.review.secretTitle: The secret is shown ONCE only
wizard.oidc.summary.runsBrowser: In the browser or on a phone (no secret, PKCE)
wizard.oidc.summary.runsServer: On its own server (with a secret)
wizard.oidc.urls.description: The application tells you this address: look for “redirect URL”, “Redirect URI” or “Callback URL” on its sign-in settings screen.
wizard.oidc.urls.heading: Where does your team come back to after identifying themselves?
wizard.oidc.urls.logoutHint: Optional. Where we take your team if they sign out from the application. If you leave it empty, they stay in Sytue.
wizard.oidc.urls.redirectHint: One per line, if the application has several (a test one, for example).
wizard.oidc.urls.slashBody: We compare the address character by character. If the application sends “…/callback” and you write “…/callback/” here, signing in will fail with “redirect_uri not registered”. Copy it exactly from the application, adding and removing nothing. It is deliberate: that exact comparison is what stops somebody diverting the sign-in somewhere else.
wizard.oidc.urls.slashTitle: The most common mistake: a slash too many or too few
